transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Hello, S-Net customer fraud prevention, Holly speaking. How can I assist you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Holly. I woke up this morning to a terrifying automated text message saying my S-Net online portal password was changed, followed by another alert saying a new secondary email was added to my profile! I didn't authorize any changes, and someone is trying to hijack my broadband and mobile account!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand how terrifying and alarming it is to receive an unexpected password change alert, Samuel. Let's secure your account and lock down all unauthorized sessions immediately.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Holly, because my saved credit card details and home address are stored inside that portal.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we access the security audit logs, could you please verify your installation address and your four-digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the address is 12 Victoria Parade, York, YO1 7EU, and the security PIN is 8024. The suspicious notification SMS arrived at zero three forty-five this morning while I was fast asleep.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for verifying those credentials, Samuel. I have initiated an immediate emergency administrative freeze on your online profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, thanks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me examine the security audit trail and access logs over the past twenty-four hours.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Did the login originate from inside the UK or abroad?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The audit log indicates a successful web portal login from an anomalous IP address located in Saint Petersburg, Russia, at three forty-four this morning.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good grief! Russia?! That confirms my account was definitely compromised by cyber criminals!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Did you click on any unsolicited SMS text links or phishing emails recently claiming your S-Net bill was unpaid or suspended?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Now that you mention it, two days ago I received a remarkably convincing text message that spoofed the official S-Net sender ID header on my phone, claiming my monthly direct debit had failed and threatening immediate broadband disconnection unless I updated my details.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: S-Net will never include direct clickable login links inside SMS billing advisory alerts; all legitimate communications advise customers to navigate independently to our secure domain.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I clicked that link in a hurry on my mobile, and it opened a webpage that looked identical to the real S-Net portal login screen.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Did that spoofed phishing webpage ask you to input your S-Net username and account password credentials?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes! I typed in my S-Net email address and my master account password before realizing the web address in the mobile browser bar was slightly misspelled, so that is exactly how they harvested my credentials!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Phishing harvesting portals capture keystrokes in real time, enabling automated credential-stuffing botnets to compromise accounts within minutes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can the attackers extract my full credit card numbers, CVV security codes, or banking sort codes from inside the billing section?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: All stored payment card numbers on our customer portal are cryptographically tokenized, displaying only the final four digits under stringent PCI-DSS compliance regulations.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is an immense relief knowing that my full debit card numbers and bank security codes were completely hidden from plain view.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please bear with me on hold for about thirty-five seconds while I trigger a global token revocation to terminate all active web and mobile app sessions.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience while holding, Samuel. All active API tokens, browser cookies, and session keys have been forcibly invalidated across our network.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does that kick the attacker out of the online account right now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, any ongoing connection attempting to communicate with our servers receives an immediate HTTP 401 unauthorized status code.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What about the unauthorized secondary email address they added to my profile?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have manually excised the fraudulent secondary recovery email address ending in mail.ru from your master contact directory, permanently removing their recovery permissions.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Excellent, so the hackers won't receive future automated password reset links or security challenge codes.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have also purged all alternate contact phone numbers and restored your authenticated primary mobile as the sole authorized verification contact across all S-Net platforms.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That closes off their unauthorized recovery backdoor completely.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Have you noticed any unauthorized hardware order requests or tariff upgrade changes submitted on the account?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, I haven't seen any order emails, but can you check if they tried ordering high-value mobile phones on my contract?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have audited the retail order queue; no handset hardware or SIM orders have been placed against your account.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is another bullet dodged, thank goodness.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have placed a high-security fraud prevention lock on your master profile, requiring mandatory telephone voice verification and security questions for any future order changes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That high-security lock will prevent any unauthorized upgrades.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us now configure a new complex password for your online portal access.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Should I create the new password over the phone or via a secure one-time SMS link?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will dispatch a cryptographically secured one-time password reset link to your authenticated mobile handset.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The text message just arrived on my phone with a secure six-digit security token.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Click that link to input your new alphanumeric password, ensuring it contains at least twelve characters, uppercase letters, numeric digits, and special punctuation symbols.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Typing in a sixteen-character random passphrase generated by my password manager containing symbols and numbers... submitted... portal says 'Password updated successfully across all systems'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The new password hash has propagated across our authentication cluster and active directory domain.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That feels significantly more secure now that the password has been completely changed.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And you should also update your primary email account password immediately, since cyber attackers frequently attempt credential stuffing across personal Google and Microsoft mailboxes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I already changed my primary Google email password on my desktop this morning using a two-factor physical security key.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That ensures your email inbox cannot be monitored by malicious actors for automated password reset notifications.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What should I do if I get another suspicious SMS text message?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Forward any fraudulent or suspicious SMS phishing messages to our national security reporting shortcode on 7726.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I have saved 7726 in my phone contacts for reporting spam.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Can you remind me what exact time that password notification SMS arrived on your handset?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: As I told you at the start of our call, it arrived at zero three forty-five this morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Samuel. I am logging that timestamp on the cybersecurity incident docket.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does S-Net support hardware security keys or authenticator app two-factor authentication?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our mobile app supports biometrics and SMS two-factor authentication.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: How is broadband performance otherwise at your residence?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Broadband speed and Wi-Fi stability have been completely fine, no dropouts or speed problems at all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am very pleased to hear your optical line connection remains healthy.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It was purely the terrifying account compromise and unauthorized Russian login that gave me such an awful scare this morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The fraud security ticket reference number logged on your profile is SEC-99120-F.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Writing that down... SEC-99120-F.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, Holly, is two-factor authentication mandatory on login now, or do I need to toggle it on in settings?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your password is reset and sessions are cleared. Have a good day. Thank you for choosing S-Net, goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, Holly, what about two-factor... hello?
